title: Physical and shared brand experiences are being positioned as a counterweight to fragmented digital attention
source_unit: Out of Home Advertising Association of America and The Harris Poll, The Power of the Human Medium: OOH Across Experiential + Retail, released September 17, 2026
geography: United States; adults ages 18-64, with Gen Z comparisons

observations.period: August 4-5, 2026; consumer preference for real-world engagement

denominator.unit: U.S. adults ages 18-64 in the report analysis; survey total 2,015 adults 18+

in_person_preference.unit: percent preferring products or retailers that engage them through in-person experiences or local outdoor events

human_feel.unit: percent saying out-of-home advertising feels more human than online or mobile advertising

cultural_relevance.unit: percent saying out-of-home advertising feels more culturally relevant than online or mobile advertising

observations.method: Online Harris Poll conducted for OAAA August 4-5, 2026; sponsored by the Foundation for Out of Home Advertising Research and Education.
observations.uncertainty: The survey is sponsor-funded industry research, and the public release does not provide the full questionnaire, weighting details or causal design; preference claims may reflect framing and self-report.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults ages 18-64, with separate Gen Z findings.
observations.counterinterpretation: Preference for in-person engagement does not prove that physical advertising outperforms digital advertising for all consumers or categories; novelty, event quality and local context may drive responses.

observations.period: August 4-5, 2026; Gen Z desire for offline social experience

denominator.unit: U.S. adults ages 18-64 in the report analysis; Gen Z is a subgroup

missing_in_person.unit: percent of Gen Z adults saying they are missing out on in-person experiences older generations had at their age

spontaneous_connection.unit: percent of Gen Z adults wanting more spontaneous moments to meet people or make friends

observations.method: Harris Poll consumer survey reported by OAAA, with Gen Z subgroup comparisons.
observations.uncertainty: These are perceptions and desires, not measures of loneliness, friendship formation, event attendance or generationally comparable behavior.
observations.subgroup: Gen Z adults in the U.S.
observations.counterinterpretation: The desire for offline connection may reflect ordinary life-stage change, pandemic memory, marketing framing or broader social conditions rather than a simple rejection of digital life.

observations.period: August 4-5, 2026; reported effects of live brand experiences

denominator.unit: U.S. adults ages 18-64 in the report analysis

memory.unit: percent saying live product or retailer events make them more likely to remember a brand

consideration.unit: percent saying experiencing a product in person makes them more likely to consider it

authenticity.unit: percent saying memorable experiences make a brand feel more authentic

event_attendance.unit: percent saying they would attend a live marketing event or promotional experience

observations.method: Online self-report survey of consumer judgments and stated behavioral intentions.
observations.uncertainty: The release reports intended or perceived effects rather than observed randomized behavior, sales lift, repeat purchase or long-term brand trust.
observations.counterinterpretation: People may express favorable attitudes toward experiences without attending or buying; event participation may be selected by consumers already inclined toward a brand.

observations.period: August 4-5, 2026; movement from physical attention to cross-channel action

denominator.unit: U.S. adults ages 18-64 in the report analysis

post_event_purchase.unit: percent of consumers who attended a live marketing event and made a purchase

post_event_search.unit: percent looking for more information after a memorable live brand experience

retail_OOH_action.value: 86% say they would take action after an interesting retail out-of-home ad; 45% would visit a website or app, 42% search online and 33% visit a store

same_day_stock_signal.unit: percent saying they would visit a nearby store the same day if an out-of-home ad indicated a product was in stock for pickup

observations.method: Harris Poll self-reported retrospective and hypothetical behavior measures across physical and digital channels.
observations.uncertainty: Reported behavior is not verified transaction data; the sponsor's industry position creates a reason to treat the magnitude of effects cautiously.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults ages 18-64 who encountered or imagined live and retail out-of-home experiences.
observations.counterinterpretation: Physical attention may be most valuable when paired with availability, timing, locality and a compelling experience; it is not a general substitute for digital discovery.

related_sources.claim: The full Harris Poll resource page exists but is restricted to OAAA members; the public press release reports the summarized findings and sample description.

boundary: This record treats sponsor-funded OOH research as a directional signal about the perceived value of physical, local and shared experiences in a fragmented attention environment. It does not establish causal advertising effectiveness, representative consumer behavior, actual sales lift, long-term trust, or that physical media is universally more human or culturally relevant than digital media.
